The 2023 governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Adamawa State, Aishatu Dahiru, has officially joined the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
The post Ex-APC governorship candidate Aisha Binani joins NDC appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria.
articles.hausa_translation: Tsohon kandidatin jagorancin APC Aisha Binani ta shiga NDC
critical_questions: What specific factors or disagreements prompted her departure from APC after being their 2023 gubernatorial candidate?
Who benefits politically from this defection—is NDC strengthening for 2027 elections or is this a personal strategic move for Binani?
Why was this defection newsworthy enough for Premium Times to report, and are there other similar party-switching stories being underreported?
What is her current political standing and influence in Adamawa State—does she retain grassroots support from her previous APC campaign?

articles.title: High cost pushes potato, meat, eggs off dining tables
articles.summary: The rise in cost of food items has forced many families to adopt dire survival strategies, including reducing protein intake, switching to cheaper substitutes, and limiting purchases to essential items only. Similarly, rising inflation and dwindling purchasing power have forced many families to adjust their consumption patterns, abandoning foreign goods and luxury food items for […]
articles.hausa_translation: Tsabar farashi na tuƙi, naman, da kwai daga teburun abinci. Karuwar farashin kayan abinci ya tilasta iyalai da su aiwatar da mahimman dabarun tsira, ciki har da rage cin protein, juyawa zuwa abin da ya fi arha, da iyakance saye zuwa abubuwan da suka zama dole kawai. Karuwar farashin kayan abinci da raguwar ikon saye sun tilasta iyalai da su canza jiyya su abinci, barin kayan gida da abubuwan luxery don gida dake kasar ta.
critical_questions: Which specific families or income groups are most affected, and why does the article lack granular data on poverty depth and regional variation?
Who benefits from rising food prices—are agricultural wholesalers, retailers, or imported goods traders profiting, and is this addressed?
What government interventions or policy responses exist, and why are they absent from this narrative of crisis?
Is the 'switching to cheaper substitutes' claim verified with examples, nutritional impact data, or health metrics from affected communities?
What timeframe defines this crisis—is this acute or chronic inflation, and how does it compare to previous price surges?

Successive governments in various states have made attempts to address the diverse problem to no avail. Pupils […]

critical_questions: Which state governments have the most resources allocated to almajiri reform, and where is that money actually going?

Is this framed as an inevitable systemic problem, when the real issue may be deliberate neglect or misaligned incentives by authorities?

articles.title: APC ‘consensus’ in crisis
articles.summary: The bid by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to decide those that will fly the party’s flag in the 2027 general elections through a consensus arrangement is experiencing hitches in many states. Our correspondents report that the process has plunged many state chapters of the APC into crisis, as governors are trying to take […]
articles.hausa_translation: APC 'yarjejeniyar' a cikin matsala: Yunwar All Progressives Congress (APC) ta niyya a yanke shawarwari game da waɗanda za su taya tutar jam'iyyar a zaben 2027 ta hanyar yarjejeniyar gama-gari, amma aiki ya shakka a jimlat jihadai. Wakilannin masu labari sun nuna cewa hali ya sa tarihin APC a jimlat jihadau zuwa waje, saboda gobernoci suna ƙoƙarin damje....
critical_questions: Which governors are driving the consensus process and what are their underlying political interests in controlling nominations?
What evidence exists that 'consensus' decisions favor incumbent power-holders over grassroots party members or aspiring candidates?
Are there documented cases of how this consensus crisis has affected party unity or member retention in specific states?
Who benefits most from a consensus system versus an open primary system, and whose voices are being excluded from this decision-making process?
What is the timeline for resolving these state-level crises before the 2027 elections, and what are the consequences if consensus fails?

articles.title: London–Lagos disruption due to bird strike – Air Peace
articles.summary: Air Peace has clarified the circumstances surrounding the disruption of its London (Gatwick) to Lagos flight on May 1, 2026, stating that the incident was caused by a bird strike. The airline’s response followed a viral video on social media alleging that passengers were stranded without communication or necessary support. Daily Trust reports that Nigerian […]
articles.hausa_translation: Air Peace ta bayyana abin da ya faru a jirgin da ke tafiya daga London zuwa Lagos a ranar 1 ga Mayu 2026, inda ta ce wani tsuntsun ya bugi jirgin. Matsalar ta bayyana bayan wani video da aka spread a social media inda aka ce fasinjoji sun jiya ba tare da sadarwa ko tallafi ba.
critical_questions: Why did Air Peace wait for viral social media outcry before issuing an official clarification about the incident?
What specific evidence corroborates the bird strike claim, and has this been independently verified by UK aviation authorities?
Were passengers adequately compensated, and what is Air Peace's liability standard for flight disruptions caused by bird strikes?
Why does the article summary cut off mid-sentence ('Nigerian […]'), and what crucial information about passenger response or regulatory action is missing?
Does Air Peace's 'clarification' address the original allegations about lack of communication and support, or does it only deflect by attributing the disruption to an external cause?
